evidence.text: Service: MEDICINE
Allergies: lisinopril
Dyspnea on Exertion
None
___ y/o male with poorly controlled type II diabetes (A1c 9.9%

___, hypertension and hyperlipidemia who was referred to ED 
with dyspnea on exertion by his PCP.

He stated that 
approximately 3 days prior to admission he eat some ___ food 
and then later became short of breath when walking down a flight 
of stairs.

On further review, he stated that he had an episode 
of bilateral arm pain approximately 10 days ago.

He was 
concerned that he might be have heart attack but did not seek 
medical attention.
The pain spontaneously resolved.

He felt that 
his acute DOE was probably due to a viral URI because he also 
had a mild cough, which he had several months prior and felt 
better with an inhaler, and decided to go to his PCP.

His PCP 
noted signs of fluid overload with bilateral lower extremity, 
decreased breath sounds.

She ordered a CXR which she was thought 
was concerning for blunting of the costophrenic angles.

EKG 
findings consistent with an anterior infarct were also 
identified.

Of note, patient has noticed intermittant swelling 
in legs over past year and intermittent abdominal discomfort 
which he attributed to gas.

He denied any recent chest 
pain/tightness, jaw discomfort or diaphoresis.

He is unsure if 
he has gained any weight.

He denied any fever, chills, night 
sweats.
In the ED, initial vitals were 99.3 96 129/88 20 97% on RA.

Exam 
notable for lower extremity edema, decreased breath sounds 
bibasilarly.

Labs notable for BNP 4143, WBC 17.7 (baseline 
mid-15), HCT 37.2.

A CXR was completed but the final read was 
pending at the time of transfer.
The pt received aspirin 243 mg
PO once.

The pt was discussed with ___ cardiology and 
admitted to ___ for congestive heart failure.
On review of systems, he denies any prior history of stroke,

TIA, deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, bleeding at the 
time of surgery, myalgias, joint pains, cough, hemoptysis, black 
stools or red stools.
He denies recent fevers, chills or rigors.
He denies exertional buttock or calf pain.

All of the other 
review of systems were negative.
1. CARDIAC RISK FACTORS: +Diabetes, +Dyslipidemia, +Hypertension
2. CARDIAC HISTORY: none
3. OTHER PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
- Diabetes Type 2 - c/b nephropathy, A1C 9.9 ___
- Hyperlipidemia
- Hypertension
- Leukocytosis
- Osteoarthritis of knee
- Obestity
- Metabolic Syndrome
Father with history of pancreatitis and possible heart attack.

No nkown family history of early MI, arrhythmia, 
cardiomyopathies, or sudden cardiac death; otherwise 
non-contributory.
Admission Exam:
GENERAL: comfortable-appearing, NAD, requesting food
HEENT: sclera anicteric, PERRL, MMM
NECK: thick, supple, unable to assess JVP due to body habitus
CARDIAC: distant heart sounds, RRR, normal S1 + S2, no m/r/g
LUNGS: distant breath sounds, bibasilar crackles
ABDOMEN: obese, soft, NTND, +BS

EXTREMITIES: ___ pitting edema in bilateral ___, distal pulses 
palpable in bilateral upper and lower extremities
SKIN: No stasis dermatitis but diffuse skin tags
PULSES:
Right: Carotid 2+ DP 2+ ___ 2+
Left: Carotid 2+ 2+ DP 2+ ___ 2+
Notable Discharge Exam:
CARDIAC: distant heart sounds, RRR, normal S1 + S2, no m/r/g
LUNGS: distant breath sounds, lungs CTAB
EXTREMITIES: trace pitting edema in bilateral ___
Admission Labs:
MCV-83 MCH-27.6 MCHC-33.5 RDW-14.5 Plt ___
___ 06:35PM BLOOD Neuts-77.5* Lymphs-15.5* Monos-4.3
Eos-2.0 Baso-0.7
___ 06:35PM BLOOD Glucose-161* UreaN-23* Creat-1.1 Na-138
K-3.7 Cl-101 HCO3-26 AnGap-15
Cardiac Labs:
___ 06:35PM BLOOD CK-MB-3 proBNP-4143*
___ 06:35PM BLOOD cTropnT-0.07*
___ 01:58AM BLOOD cTropnT-0.06*
___ 12:25PM BLOOD CK-MB-3 cTropnT-0.06*
Serial EKGs:
1. ___ (Tracing 1): Normal sinus rhythm.
Q waves with slight
ST segment elevation in leads V1-V4.
Inverted T waves in leads
I, aVL and V5-V6.
No previous tracing available for comparison.
Prior anterior wall myocardial infarction of indeterminate age.
2. ___ (Tracing 2): Normal sinus rhythm.
Compared to tracing
#1 no diagnostic interval change.
3. ___ (Tracing 3): Normal sinus rhythm.

Compared to 
tracings #1 and #2 no diagnostic interval change.

Tracing 
continues to show the pattern of a prior anterior wall 
myocardial infarction of indeterminate age.

Consider possible 
prior inferior myocardial infarction.
Bilateral pleural effusions are small, and layering.

Heart size 
is normal.
Lungs are clear.

Fullness in the right 
tracheobronchial angle of the 
mediastinum could be due to venous engorgement, but raised 
concern for 
adenopathy.

Prior chest radiographs would need to be obtained to 
see if this is a new finding warranting further investigation 
with CT scanning.
The left atrium is mildly dilated.

There is mild symmetric left 
ventricular hypertrophy with normal cavity size.

There is severe 
regional left ventricular systolic dysfunction with Severe 
hypokinesis of the distal ___ of the inferior and 
inferolateral walls, anterior wall and septum.

The apex is 
mildly aneurysmal and mildly dyskinetic.

The estimated cardiac 
index is normal (>=2.5L/min/m2).

No masses or thrombi are seen 
in the left ventricle.

Tissue Doppler imaging suggests a normal 
left ventricular filling pressure (PCWP<12mmHg).

Right 
ventricular chamber size and free wall motion are normal.

The 
diameters of aorta at the sinus, ascending and arch levels are 
normal.

The aortic valve leaflets (3) are mildly thickened but 
aortic stenosis is not present.
No aortic regurgitation is seen.
The mitral valve leaflets are structurally normal.

There is no 
mitral valve prolapse.
Mild (1+) mitral regurgitation is seen.
There is mild pulmonary artery systolic hypertension.

There is 
no pericardial effusion.

IMPRESSION: Mild symmetric left 
ventricular hypertrophy with normal cavity size and extensive 
regional systolic dysfunction c/w multivessel CAD or other 
diffuse process.
Mild mitral regurgitation.

Pulmonary artery 
systolic hypertension.
Myocardial Viability Study (___):
The left ventricular cavity size is moderately enlarged.

Resting 
perfusion images at 20 minutes reveal a severe perfusion defect 
involving the anterior wall and apex.

This defect persists at 4 
hours and 24 
hours, without redistribution.

No prior studies are available 
for comparison at ___.

IMPRESSION: Severe left ventricular 
perfusion defect involving the anterior wall and apex, fixed at

4 and 24 hours without redistribution; most consistent with 
non-viable myocardium.
Discharge Labs:
MCV-84 MCH-28.5 MCHC-34.1 RDW-15.0 Plt ___
___ 06:20AM BLOOD Glucose-96 UreaN-19 Creat-0.9 Na-140
K-3.9 Cl-102 HCO3-28 AnGap-___ y/o male with poorly controllled DM2 (A1c 9.9% in ___, HTN,

HLD, but no known history of CAD, who presented with dyspnea on 
exertion and lower extremity edema consistent with new-onset CHF 
in the setting of EKG changes concerning for missed anterior MI.
EKG revealed Q waves concerning for ___ infarct.

Troponin-T was 0.06 on admission and CK-MB was within normal 
limits, which further supported the possibility of a missed 
event in the preceding week to 10 days.

TTE revealed mild 
symmetric left ventricular hypertrophy with normal cavity size 
and extensive regional systolic dysfunction c/w multivessel CAD 
or other diffuse process and an EF of ___.

A myocardial 
viability study revealed a severe left ventricular perfusion 
defect involving the anterior wall and apex, fixed at 4 and 24 
hours without redistribution, which was most consistent with 
non-viable myocardium.

He was diuresed with Lasix IV boluses to 
clinical euvolemia and was started on Lasix 20 mg daily prior to 
discharge.
His Losartan-HCTZ was disconinued and Valsartan 80 mg

BID was started given research findings supporting better 
outcomes in heart failure.

He was also started on Metoprolol 
which was titrated to Metoprolol succinate 100 mg daily at 
discharge.

Spironolactone was initiated at 12.5 mg daily and was 
continued at discharge.

Lastly, Coumadin was started given risk 
of thromboembolism.

His Simvastatin was continued at his home 
dose as his LDL was 68.
Transition Issues:

1. Titration of Metoprolol, Valsartan and Sprionolactone to 
clinical trial targets, as patient tolerates
2. Repeat TTE in 3 months for consideration of ICD placement
Other Issues by Problem:

Chronic Leukocytosis: Review of records indicates chronic for 
several years and below reported baseline on admission.

Patient 
was without infectious symptoms.

CXR was negative for an 
infiltrate/consolidation.

Patient denies any B symptoms (no 
night sweats, no weight loss, no malaise).

Urinalysis and 
culture were negative.
Patient was continued on his home Glargine and received an
Humalog insulin sliding scale.

Metformin was held during 
admission.

Hydrochlorothiazide, in setting of medication changes as above, 
but also for any potential contribution to hyperglycemia.
Hyperlipidemia: LDL 68, at goal (<70).

Patient was continued 
on his home dose of Simvastatin 40 mg daily.

Hypertension: Blood pressure less than 130/80 throughout most 
of admission.
Anti-hypertensives adjusted as above.
MEDICATIONS:
1. Glargine 65 units qhs
2. Inslin Aspart 19 units with meals
3. Metformin 1500 mg daily
4. Simvastatin 40 mg daily
5. Losartan-HCTZ 100-25 mg daily
6. Fluticasone 110 mcg ___ puffs twice daily x 2 weeks
7. Multivitamin daily
8. Aspirin 81 mg daily
9. Fish Oil
Mental Status: Clear and coherent.
Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - Independent.
PA and lateral chest reviewed in the absence of prior chest radiographs:
Bilateral pleural effusions are small, and layering.
Heart size is normal.
Lungs are clear.
Fullness in the right tracheobronchial angle of the mediastinum could be due to venous engorgement, but raised concern for adenopathy.
Prior chest radiographs would need to be obtained to see if this is a new finding warranting further investigation with CT scanning.
Physical Therapy: 1 order(s) before T_pa; first on hospital day 2, most recent 24.5 h before T_pa.
